title: Complete guide to cows
summary: A humorous collection of ASCII-art drawings of cows, assembled and circulated as an informal file in the late 1980s. Each entry pairs a small text-drawn cow with a witty caption, and the pieces are grouped loosely by theme. Some cows are parodies of famous people, films, and places: a cow belonging to George Washington, a cow lived with Dr. Doolittle, a cow sunning at Fort Lauderdale, a cow skiing at Aspen, a cow jumping over the Moon, and a cow on the Red Baron's list of casualties. Others play on puns and everyday situations, such as a cow in heat, a cow chewing marbles, a cow in an Argyle sweater, and a Freshman cow gaining weight over the years. The file also includes a few bull jokes, a psychologist-and-patient gag, and cows named after Elvis, Mrs. O'Leary's fire, and Dracula. Editorial notes invite readers to submit their own cow drawings and jokes by e-mail, and the file is presented as freely distributable. The whole thing is short, light, and meant to be read in a few minutes.
